## Purpose and Entry Points
NodeCast TV is a self-hosted web IPTV player for live channels, EPG, VOD movies, and series. The Node/Express process serves the API and static browser client from `server/index.js`; browser bootstrapping occurs through `public/index.html`, `public/js/app.js`, and the separate login page `public/login.html`.

## Client Application
The frontend is vanilla ES6 JavaScript, with page controllers for major content modes and reusable playback/navigation components. `public/js/api.js` is the client boundary to backend APIs; `public/js/auth.js` manages client authentication state. Routing/rendering fans into:
- Live/watch: `public/js/pages/LivePage.js`, `public/js/pages/WatchPage.js`, `public/js/components/VideoPlayer.js`
- Guide: `public/js/pages/Guide.js`, `public/js/components/EpgGuide.js`
- VOD and sources/settings: `public/js/pages/MoviesPage.js`, `public/js/pages/SeriesPage.js`, `public/js/pages/Settings.js`

## Authentication and Authorization
Authentication is implemented at the server boundary, including local users, roles, and optional OIDC SSO. Core authorization/session logic resides in `server/auth.js`; auth endpoints are exposed by `server/routes/auth.js`, while administrative user operations are in `server/routes/users.js`. OIDC integrates with an external identity provider such as Authentik or Keycloak via configured issuer/client/callback values.

## Persistent Content Model
SQLite is the application’s durable store, intended to live in the mounted `data/` volume in container deployments. `server/db/sqlite.js` owns database connection/schema behavior, with `server/db.js` as a database access layer. It persists users, configured IPTV sources, normalized catalog/EPG content, preferences, favorites, and viewing history, surfaced through routes such as `server/routes/sources.js`, `server/routes/favorites.js`, and `server/routes/history.js`.

## Source Ingestion and Synchronization
IPTV providers enter through source-management APIs and are normalized into the local catalog. `server/routes/sources.js` controls configured M3U and Xtream sources; `server/services/syncService.js` orchestrates refreshes. Parsers/adapters isolate provider formats:
- M3U parsing: `server/services/m3uParser.js`
- Xtream-to-M3U adaptation and provider access: `server/services/m3uXtreamAdapter.js`, `server/services/xtreamApi.js`
- XMLTV/EPG parsing: `server/services/epgParser.js`
Catalog queries for frontend browsing and guide rendering are served by `server/routes/channels.js`.

## Stream Delivery and Media Processing
Playback is mediated by backend endpoints when direct browser delivery is unsuitable. `server/routes/proxy.js` provides a CORS/mixed-content-safe stream proxy. `server/routes/probe.js` examines source media; `server/routes/remux.js` handles container remuxing; `server/routes/transcode.js` creates browser-compatible output. `server/services/transcodeSession.js` manages FFmpeg work/session lifecycle, and `server/services/hwDetect.js` selects or reports software versus NVENC, AMF, QuickSync, or VAAPI acceleration. The browser player in `public/js/components/VideoPlayer.js` consumes HLS-oriented output.

## Runtime and Deployment Boundaries
The runtime is Node.js 14+ with Express, SQLite via better-sqlite3, browser-side HLS.js, and host/container FFmpeg. Docker packaging and persistence are defined in `Dockerfile` and `docker-compose.yml`; GPU device/runtime access is an optional infrastructure dependency for hardware encoding. IPTV servers, EPG feeds, OIDC providers, and optional reverse proxies remain external systems accessed across HTTP.
